holidays.name: International Youth Day
holidays.description: A UN-designated day that celebrates young people and spotlights the issues they face, from education to employment. Expect panels, youth-led projects, and plenty of hashtag activism.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly officially designated August 12 as International Youth Day in 1999, following a recommendation from the 1998 World Conference of Ministers Responsible for Youth in Lisbon.
holidays.funFact: Each year has a different theme, and the UN uses the day to push governments to include young people in decision-making.

holidays.name: World Elephant Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the planet's largest land animals and rally support against poaching, habitat loss, and the ivory trade. Participants share elephant photos, donate to sanctuaries, and trumpet their love for big ears.
holidays.origin: Launched in 2012 by Canadian filmmakers Patricia Sims and Michael Clark of the Elephant Reintroduction Foundation, together with Sivaporn Dardarananda of the Elephant Reintroduction Foundation of Thailand.
holidays.funFact: Elephants are among the few animals known to use tools, and they can recognize themselves in a mirror.

holidays.name: National Julienne Fries Day
holidays.description: A salute to the skinny, crispy, matchstick-cut cousin of the regular french fry. It's a perfect excuse to argue about whether thinner means crunchier, and whether ketchup is mandatory.
holidays.origin: An unofficial American food holiday that appears on August 12 in many food-holiday calendars. It honors the julienne cut, a classic French culinary technique for slicing food into long, thin strips.
holidays.funFact: The word 'julienne' has been used in French cooking since at least the 1700s, and the cut is traditionally about 3 mm thick and 5 cm long.

holidays.name: Middle Child Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the often overlooked middle sibling, who is stuck between the responsible oldest and the adored youngest. Middle children are encouraged to finally get their moment in the spotlight.
holidays.origin: An informal, family-centered observance that has circulated for decades, and it is popular on social media thanks to the long-running stereotype of 'middle child syndrome.' It is often said to have been started by a woman named Elizabeth Walker in 1986, though that detail is murky.
holidays.funFact: Many famous people were middle children, including Abraham Lincoln, Bill Gates, and Madonna, which is a favorite talking point on this day.

holidays.name: Vinyl Record Day
holidays.description: A day for crate-diggers and audiophiles to dust off the turntable and celebrate the warm crackle of vinyl. People host listening parties and swap record-hunting stories.
holidays.origin: Vinyl Record Day is observed on August 12 because it commemorates the date in 1877 when Thomas Edison is said to have completed his first phonograph, the invention that started recorded sound. It was founded by Gary Freiberg.
holidays.funFact: Edison's first recording is traditionally said to have been 'Mary Had a Little Lamb' recited by the inventor himself, on tinfoil-wrapped cylinder.
